title: Compact offline prefetch protocol and SDK rightsizing notes
content:
Context and motivation:

We frequently get requests to make the Hosted API usable in constrained network environments (mobile with intermittent connectivity, enterprise apps behind flaky proxies, edge devices with periodic connectivity windows). Many of our streaming/partial-output patterns are optimized for always-online, low-latency clients; but real apps need a first-class pattern for: prefetching tool outputs, generating compact serialized checkpoints for resumable sessions, and letting SDKs gracefully rightsizing their resource use when offline.

This doc is an engineering-first PRD-sketch: a compact offline-prefetch protocol plus SDK ergonomics guidance to: reduce perceived latency for mobile users, allow deterministic retry / resume, and limit token/network cost by right-sizing when offline. Intention: not a full spec of streaming frames (we reuse our existing compact-frame wire format), but a narrow set of primitives and SDK patterns to ship as an opt-in feature in hosted API v2.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce median time-to-first-action for mobile tool-heavy flows by >= 40% (compared to baseline on first cold load).
- Ensure resumable sessions can recover with <= 1 additional round-trip on reconnect for typical tool graphs (<=3 tool calls).
- Keep additional server-side storage footprint per session < 250KB (compact checkpoints).
- Expose telemetry signals for prefetch success/failure and reconstruction quality.

Constraints and tradeoffs:
- Prefetch must not leak sensitive data: prefetch should respect prompt redaction policies and tenant-level privacy flags.
- SDKs must be conservative by default (opt-in prefetch).
- Prefetch can increase upstream cost; give customers controls to cap spending and TTLs.
- We must support mixed-mode: streaming clients continue to work; prefetch targets intermittent clients.

High-level design overview:
- Prefetch intent: client indicates a small set of future tool calls or completion intents it wants to precompute (e.g., "summarize last N messages", "lookup:customer_contacts(customer_id=123)").
- Server evaluates prefetch intents under a policy sandbox and returns a compact checkpoint (serialized delta frames + tool outputs) that the client can apply offline to render partial or full UI responses.
- Checkpoint format is intentionally small: compressed JSONL with locked-down schemas and optional binary blobs for attachments (base64).
- Checkpoint metadata includes: model version, seed prompt hash, approximate token cost estimate, ttl, and minimal telemetry tags for attribution.

Wire primitives (sketch):
1) prefetch.create (HTTP POST /v2/prefetch)
   - body: {session_id, intents: [ {id, type, canonical_args, quality_budget}, allow_tool_calls: bool, privacy_level } , client_capabilities}
   - response: {prefetch_id, status: queued | ready | rejected, estimate: {tokens, cost_usd}, eta_seconds}
2) prefetch.fetch (GET /v2/prefetch/{prefetch_id})
   - returns checkpoint if ready; 304 style response if client provides if-none-match with checkpoint-hash
3) prefetch.apply (client-side only)
   - SDK helper: applyCheckpoint(checkpoint) -> returns rendered fragments + validation warnings
4) prefetch.invalidate (DELETE /v2/prefetch/{prefetch_id})
   - invalidates server-side cached checkpoint earlier than TTL (user logout, data revocation)

Checkpoint content (compact schema):
- header: {prefetch_id, model, seq_hash, created_at, ttl_seconds, privacy_tags}
- frames: [ compact-frame-string, ... ]  (reuses our compact frame encoding for progressive partial results)
- tools: [ {tool_id, call_args, tool_status, output_hash, compact_output_summary} ]
- attachments: optional base64 small blobs (images, csv) with size cap 64KB each
- signature: server-signed hmac for client verification

Security and privacy guardrails:
- Prefetch must be disabled for sessions flagged with sensitive scope (PII-high) unless enterprise has explicitly allowed with policy (KMS-backed consent).
- All tool outputs in checkpoints must go through the same safety/redaction pipeline as live tool calls; additionally, we tag outputs with redaction_score.
- Default TTL is 1h; enterprise settings can increase up to 24h.
- Invalidate on explicit user data deletion requests (API to customer tenant admin).

SDK ergonomics (mobile-first):
- Opt-in surface: client declares at route initialization whether it accepts prefetch and a per-route budget cap. Example API:
  const session = Redwood.session({id: 'chat:123', allowPrefetch: true, prefetchBudgetTokens: 150});
  const preview = await session.prefetch([{type: 'summary', args:{n:50}}]);

- Local store: SDK persists checkpoints in a small local LRU store (default limit 3 checkpoints or 512KB). Checkpoints are validated by signature before use.

- Fallback model: when offline, SDK tries to apply latest checkpoint and renders optimistic UI; any interactive tool call that requires freshness falls back to queued mode and sends a minimal wakeup ping when connectivity resumes.

- Rightsizing heuristics: SDK monitors network RTT and battery level and adjusts prefetch aggressiveness. Rough heuristic: avoid prefetch when device battery < 20% unless user explicitly requested. Provide hooks for app to override: session.setPrefetchPolicy({aggressive: false}).

- Developer UX: provide small helpers for typical patterns:
  - prefetchSummarizeRecent(messages, {budgetTokens: 120})
  - prefetchToolGraph([{toolId: 'db.search', args}, {toolId: 'fmt'}, ...])
  - onCheckpointApplied(callback(meta, fragments))

Server-side execution semantics and billing:
- Prefetch executes as best-effort with QoS deprioritization; customers may purchase reserved prefetch capacity in Dedicated to guarantee low-latency prefetch preparation for large fleets.
- Billing: prefetch tokens billed at a lower "prefetch" rate by default (discount to encourage), but customers may opt-out to avoid speculative spend. Prefetch cost shown in response estimate and in Console usage UI.

Telemetry and observability (must be instrumented):
- Signals emitted per prefetch: prefetch.requested, prefetch.queued, prefetch.started, prefetch.success, prefetch.rejected, prefetch.applied, prefetch.invalidated
- Important metadata: tenant_id, session_id, sdk_platform, network_state (online/offline/weak), cost_estimate_usd, actual_cost_usd, model, tool_ids
- Console surface: per-tenant prefetch spend, hit-rate (checkpoint applied vs. requested), reconstruction failures (mismatch hashes), average checkpoint size distribution

Operational concerns and rate limits:
- Rate limiting: soft limit 10 prefetch requests per session per minute; global tenant-level soft cap with alerting.
- Storage TTL cleanup job: background sweeper to remove expired checkpoints; support immediate purge on policy change
- Abuse cases: a malicious client could request combinatorially many prefetch intents — mitigate by per-tenant cost caps and per-session concurrency limits

Compatibility with streaming and tool-calling primitives:
- Prefetch uses same compact-frame representation so clients can reuse the streaming rendering pipeline offline. That keeps code paths shared and reduces testing burden.
- Prefetch tooling must honor tool-side idempotency markers; serialized tool outputs include tool-call ids so that when the client reconnects and replays, the server can detect duplicates and avoid double-execution where possible.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) internal alpha: enable for Redwood employees only, no billing, logs to internal datadog dashboard. Test device diversity and failure modes (battery, proxies).
2) invite-only customer pilot: 2–3 customers (mix: consumer mobile app, enterprise field ops) with explicit billing disabled. Collect UX feedback & telemetry.
3) general availability (opt-in): release SDK helpers across JS/Android/iOS; prefetch appears in Console with toggles, billing visible and default discount applied.
4) GA+ (enterprise): support configurable TTLs, KMS policy allow-list, reserved prefetch capacity for Dedicated customers.

Migration and dev tasks (rough):
- SDK: JS, Android, iOS impl of checkpoint store + apply helpers (owner: devexp)
- Server: prefetch queue microservice + storage layer + signer (owner: serving-runtime)
- Console: prefetch settings UI + per-tenant spend panel (owner: product-console)
- Billing: expose prefetch tokens at separate ledger code path (owner: finance)
- Security: hook into redaction pipeline and admin invalidation API (owner: security)

Open questions (action items):
- Exact compact-frame delta encoding: do we require a new thin header to support checkpoints or reuse streaming frames verbatim? (owner: serving-runtime)
- How do we reconcile prefetched tool outputs with eventual live tool-call idempotency when the caller replays the same action after reconnect? (owner: applied-ml)
- TTL defaults: 1h vs 4h for poor connectivity regions — what does ops think about storage/cleanup costs? (owner: infra)
- Should prefetch results be materialized in tenant-local S3 for large attachments or kept in our blobstore? (owner: infra+security)

Quick checklist for next meeting:
- [ ] agree on prefetch API contract and minimal required fields
- [ ] list of pilot customers and opt-in criteria
- [ ] decide on server-side storage backends and retention SLA
- [ ] finalize telemetry schema and Console visuals
- [ ] security review on PII and KMS gating

Notes to self / rough implementation hints:
- Keep checkpoint signature verification lightweight (HMAC with tenant key) so SDKs can validate offline without PK lookups.
- Use zstd on frames and gzip fallback for older clients. Avoid bespoke binary formats to reduce SDK friction.
- Provide a shim in SDK to convert checkpoint frames into the same UI render pipeline used for streaming (frame -> token actions -> render).

Appendix: example prefetch request (informal)
POST /v2/prefetch
{
  "session_id": "chat:123",
  "intents": [
    {"id":"sum1","type":"summarize","canonical_args":{"n":40},"quality_budget":0.7 },
    {"id":"lookup1","type":"tool_call","canonical_args":{"tool":"db.search","q":"customer:123"},"allow_tool_calls":true}
  ],
  "client_capabilities": {"platform":"ios","store_checkpoint":true}
}

We should keep this doc intentionally narrow (prefetch primitives + SDK patterns). Link to streaming contract doc for frame-level details.

-- Aisha
